resp.t:
**Python: yes, it's needed, so I uninstalled nothing.** The four ruflo plugins themselves run on Node, but other plugins you have installed run Python scripts as hooks, and there are 7,406 `.py` files under `~/.claude/plugins` alone.

What is installed is Python 3.14.7 (64-bit) plus the Python Launcher (`py.exe`), both under `AppData\Local\Programs\Python`.

Deleting every `.py` file on the machine would break more than Claude Code plugins. Other applications bundle their own Python scripts, and there is no way to undo it short of reinstalling each one. If you still want Python gone, the safe version is to uninstall only the two programs above and leave `.py` files alone; the Python-based plugin hooks would then fail on every prompt.

One of them already does: a hook reported "Python was not found" this turn. It most likely calls `python3`, which on your machine points only to the Microsoft Store placeholder rather than the real install.

**Node.js: the 39 `node.exe` processes are all MCP servers started by this Claude Code session.** Each plugin that provides tools launches its own server, for example MongoDB, GitKraken, Pinecone, JProfiler, SAP Fiori, WordPress and Chrome DevTools.

- **Why so many:** servers launched through `npx` show up as two processes each (the launcher and the server itself).
- **Cost:** about 825 MB of memory in total.
- **Lifetime:** they should exit when you close Claude Code; none of them is installed as a background service.

The way to cut them down is to disable plugins you don't use via `/plugin`. Say so if you want a list of which plugin owns which server, or if you want me to go ahead with the Python uninstall.

None of these stop-hook checks call for action: no files or code were changed this session, nothing was worth persisting, and no deal workflow is in progress.

The Python and Node.js findings above stand. Nothing was uninstalled; the Python uninstall and the plugin-to-server list are still yours to call.

Nothing to add: no files were modified, so the attestation note doesn't apply. The open question is still whether you want Python uninstalled or the list of which plugin owns which Node server.
